newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. rice exports to Asia seen rosy - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rice exports to Asia seen rosy - USDA.

text.p: U.S. rice exports to Asia look promising especially if Japan and South Korea honour market liberalisation commitments, an agricultural economist with the U.S. Agriculture Department (USDA) said on Friday.

"The future looks full of promise for United States exports (of rice) to Asia," Morgan Perkins, economist with the USDA's Foreign Agricultural Service, said in a report to the Asia rice conference in Singapore.

"As long as nations like Japan and South Korea continue to honour their market liberalisation commitments and economic growth continues to expand high-quality rice markets throughout eastern Asia, demand growth is expected to continue strong," he said.

Attention to quality by U.S. rice farmers in production and processing has had the effect of opening up exports to other Southeast Asian markets like Singapore and Indonesia. Hong Kong has also taken in some rice from the United States.
U.S. rice exports in 1996 to Japan will probably hit around 450,000 tonnes while South Korea is expected to reach about 100,000 tonnes.
In 1997, anticipated Japanese imports of U.S. medium grain rice may touch 600,000 tonnes and hit a peak of over 750,000 tonnes by 2000. Korean purchases should touch over 200,000 tonnes by 2000.

"Increasing demand in Asia combined with steady exports to the Middle East, Canada and Europe provide a foreign outlet for U.S. production," Perkins said. "Rising internal demand also supports increased medium-grain planting."
